note: Assumptions for the compliance cost of each requirement (DECISIONS E-700). A requirement's cost a year is the staff time it takes, valued at the Office of Impact Analysis's work rate, for the businesses it binds: hours when a business starts (or first becomes bound) times the new businesses a year, plus hours each year times the businesses operating. Hours come from the requirement's kind unless 'overrides' or the licence costs (licence-costs.json) give them for that requirement. Every hours figure under 'kinds' is assumed: no regulator or Office of Impact Analysis publication gives standard hours for these tasks. An 'overrides' entry takes its figures from a source for one requirement, and may count the entities bound from a regulator's list in place of the ABS counts ('entities'); its basis says what was sourced and what assumed (DECISIONS E-701). Replace a row's hours, and its basis, when a sourced figure is found. Drafted by AI-assisted desk research; not yet checked by a person.

licence.task: Apply for the licence, then renew it
licence.basis: Assumed, as for the licence costs (E-175): an application means gathering identity, qualification and insurance documents and completing the form; a renewal, taken as yearly, is mostly an online payment.

registration.task: Register, then keep the details up to date
registration.basis: Assumed: most registrations are a short online form; updating details is occasional.

approval.task: Prepare and lodge an application for approval
approval.basis: Assumed: an approval is sought for each project, premises or product, so it is counted as one application a year for each business bound. Plans, reports and fees paid to consultants are not counted.

notification.basis: Assumed: one notice a year, mostly a short form.

reporting.task: Prepare and lodge a report or return
reporting.basis: Assumed: one report or return a year. Reports the law requires more often, or audited reports, cost more.

record-keeping.task: Keep the records the law requires
record-keeping.basis: Assumed: about an hour a month (central), from 5 hours to half an hour a week.

tax-or-levy.task: Work out and pay the tax, levy or fee (the time, not the amount)
tax-or-levy.basis: Assumed: from one yearly payment to a monthly or quarterly return. The amount paid is a transfer to government and is left out (Regulatory Burden Measurement Framework, p. 4).

insurance.task: Arrange and renew the insurance (the time, not the premium)
insurance.basis: Assumed: a yearly renewal. The premium is a substantive cost and is not counted.

standard.task: Learn the standard and check the business meets it (paperwork and checking only)
standard.basis: Assumed: keeping up with the standard and checking against it. The cost of meeting it (equipment, building work, training) is not counted.

other.task: Not costed: the obligation varies too much to assume hours
other.basis: No default: hours are assumed only where the obligation's kind says what the business does.

cth-financial-accountability-regime.task: Register accountable persons with APRA and ASIC, keep accountability maps and statements up to date, notify changes, and defer senior executives' variable pay
cth-financial-accountability-regime.basis: Sourced, from the impact statement for the Banking Executive Accountability Regime (BEAR), which the Financial Accountability Regime (FAR) replaced: Treasury estimated BEAR would cost $11.5 million a year for 149 authorised deposit-taking institutions (4 large, 20 medium, 125 small), upfront costs included, and the Office of Best Practice Regulation agreed the estimate. That is $77,181 an institution a year, taken here as 843 hours at today's work rate. It is in 2017 prices and not indexed. FAR also binds insurers and superannuation trustees, each assumed to cost the same as an average institution under BEAR. The low and high values (half and double) are assumed. No impact analysis costed FAR itself: its explanatory memorandum relies on the Royal Commission's final report, certified in place of one.
